The main takeaway from our work is that

the association between energy intake and mortality is not linear, and that the association between low energy intake and mortality in the Japanese is not as clear-cut as it has been in previous studies.
the total energy intake is not a risk factor for mortality in Japan.

the total amount of energy consumed is an important factor in predicting mortality, and that the amount of calories consumed is more important than the source of the calories, whether they come from fats, carbohydrates, or proteins.
